sources.mode: Rule that fixes the roll of the club head about the shaft, the one head angle the shaft markers of a capture do not observe. "address_square" (default, OSV-8 #11755) keeps the roll at which the face points down the target line at the captured address pose. "design_loft_at_address" (#15150) solves the roll at which the static loft at the address pose equals the head's design loft (or the spec club block's "design_loft_deg"); the address face angle is then whatever the measured shaft direction leaves. Both are assumptions about how the golfer set the club down: no marker of the capture locates the face on the head, so neither is a measurement, and neither changes a fitted joint angle. Measured on the matched driver swing of 2026-11-20 (10.5 degree head of 56 degree lie on a shaft 41.9 degrees above the ground at address): address_square gives address face +3.2 degrees and static loft 18.7 degrees; design_loft_at_address turns the head a further 11.6 degrees and gives address face -5.1 degrees and static loft 10.5 degrees. Carried to impact by the rotation of the captured head marker triad alone (no fit), at the sample where the captured head speed drops from 48.8 to 35.8 m/s: address_square gives a face about 9 degrees open to the head path with about 19 to 20 degrees of dynamic loft, design_loft_at_address a face within about 1 degree of the path with about 13 degrees of dynamic loft. The second is what a solid driver strike looks like, which supports that mode without proving it; one capture, one club.
